analysis.headline: Colombia carries out the sixth bombing of De la Espriella's government, killing six

analysis.says_vs_does: De la Espriella announced the strike in advance and called it very important and strategic. Outlets disagree on the target: Caracol places it in Chocó against the Clan del Golfo, while one El Tiempo report names Mordisco's dissidents.
analysis.follow_the_money: Sources do not give a figure.
analysis.at_stake: The president gains a show of force after loosening some restrictions on bombings, Yahoo Noticias reports. La FM reports that an earlier bombing in his term killed four dissidents, including a 16-year-old.
tensions: Colombian state vs Clan del Golfo and FARC dissidents: air strikes have returned as a routine tool under the new government.

analysis.headline: Chilean police arrest three members of Las Águilas, a Tren de Aragua faction, over a kidnapping and murder in Puente Alto
analysis.what_happened: Chile's PDI arrested two Venezuelans and a Chilean over the kidnapping and killing of a 45-year-old woman found in a Puente Alto camp, BioBío and Cooperativa report. Four jailed suspects face new charges.
analysis.says_vs_does: The Clinic reports the faction's members came from earlier Tren de Aragua cells dismantled in other cases. Arrests have broken cells without ending the brand, which regroups under new names.
analysis.follow_the_money: Sources do not give a figure.
analysis.at_stake: Kast's government faces pressure as Justice Minister Rabat confronts a constitutional accusation over sentence reductions for Tren de Aragua extortionists. The case undercuts its hard-line message.
tensions: Kast government vs opposition: a tough-on-crime government is accused of softening sentences for Tren de Aragua members.

analysis.headline: Rio police target a Comando Vermelho gas-cylinder monopoly as Mato Grosso do Sul arrests PCC and CV members
analysis.what_happened: Operação Dominus targeted a Comando Vermelho group in Rio de Janeiro that imposed a monopoly on cooking gas, G1 reports. In Mato Grosso do Sul, police served 20 arrest warrants over the PCC-CV dispute.
analysis.says_vs_does: The record shows the CV acting as a tax and market authority in areas it controls, forcing traders to meet sales targets. This goes beyond drug trafficking into control of household goods.
analysis.follow_the_money: The group charged 150 reais per gas cylinder and set sales quotas for merchants, G1 reports. Sources do not give a total revenue figure.
analysis.at_stake: The CV draws steady income from residents regardless of drug markets. Brazilian police seek to cut that revenue, while the PCC and CV compete for territory in Mato Grosso do Sul.
tensions: PCC vs Comando Vermelho: the MS investigation identified 22 people involved in the two factions' dispute.

analysis.headline: US charges 24 in a Sinaloa-linked Tennessee network run from state prisons, as CBP reports large port seizures
analysis.what_happened: US prosecutors charged 24 members of a network linked to the Sinaloa Cartel that distributed meth, fentanyl and cocaine in Tennessee, Infobae reports. CBP seized nearly 1,600 pounds of meth at Otay Mesa.
analysis.says_vs_does: US authorities link the Tennessee network to the Sinaloa Cartel. Sources name no faction, and two leaders allegedly ran it from state prisons, which points to local control.
analysis.follow_the_money: CBP valued the Otay Mesa meth at 2.5 million dollars and a Brownsville cocaine load at 611,000 dollars. Seizure values are agency estimates and measure enforcement as well as traffic.
analysis.at_stake: US prosecutors show reach into retail distribution. Commercial trucks at ports of entry remain the documented crossing method in these cases.
tensions: US enforcement vs cartel supply: seizures concentrate at commercial crossings in California and Texas.

analysis.headline: Marina kills Chuy González Peñuelas, Cártel de Guasave figure wanted by the US, in northern Sinaloa
analysis.what_happened: Navy forces killed Jesús González Peñuelas, alias Chuy González, after a pursuit in Siete Ejidos, Guasave, according to Ríodoce and El País. Security Secretary García Harfuch said two men died and identification awaits genetic and fingerprint tests.
analysis.says_vs_does: Harfuch places him in the Cártel de Guasave under Fausto Isidro Meza. Outlets report he worked for both the Chapitos and the Mayiza, so his allegiance in the civil war is contested.
analysis.follow_the_money: The US offered a reward of 5 million dollars. Expansión reports that US authorities linked him in May to drug trafficking and laundering for the Sinaloa Cartel; sources do not give laundering figures.
analysis.at_stake: Mexico gains a high-value result on a US most-wanted target before federal security chiefs tour Sinaloa. His network's northern Sinaloa heroin and fentanyl production loses a senior manager.
tensions: Chapitos vs Mayiza: outlets disagree on which faction González Peñuelas served when he died.

analysis.headline: Chihuahua governor accuses Morena leader Ariadna Montiel of crime ties, and the Security Cabinet denies any intelligence report
analysis.what_happened: Chihuahua Governor Maru Campos told Carlos Loret that Morena leader Ariadna Montiel has ties to organised crime, citing a meeting involving El Guano. The federal Security Cabinet denied the meeting and any intelligence report.
analysis.says_vs_does: Both sides offer claims, not evidence. Campos has shown no documents in sources, and the federal denial came by social-media message; Montiel is preparing three legal complaints against Campos.
analysis.follow_the_money: Sources do not give a figure.
analysis.at_stake: Campos gains a national platform against Morena in a state contested by Sinaloa factions. Montiel and the federal government seek to contain a narco-politics charge against the ruling party.
tensions: Chihuahua government vs federal government: the PAN governor and Morena trade accusations, and Guanajuato's PAN governor declined to back Campos.

analysis.headline: US authorities arrest 10 alleged Sinaloa Cartel members in Florida over a Mexico-to-Tampa Bay cocaine pipeline
analysis.what_happened: US authorities arrested 10 alleged members of a Sinaloa Cartel affiliate in Florida, including cell number two Erick Manuel Gómez Tapia, alias El Canelo. CBS12 describes a cocaine pipeline from Mexico to Tampa Bay.
analysis.says_vs_does: US authorities call the cell a Sinaloa Cartel affiliate. Milenio notes that no cell name has been released and nothing ties it to the Chapitos or the Mayiza.
analysis.follow_the_money: CBS12 values the bust at 30 million dollars. Sources do not show how proceeds moved back to Mexico.
analysis.at_stake: US prosecutors show reach into cartel distribution inside the United States. The affiliate loses its Florida distribution cell.
tensions: US enforcement vs Sinaloa distribution: arrests hit the retail end of the supply chain, not its Mexican command.
